statement: In the Chicago Loop, the Monday/Friday deficit in 'L' station entries, relative to Tuesday to Thursday, rose from 2019 to the 12 months to October 2026 by about as many percentage points as the New York CBD deficit did (8.7 points, 6.9 to 10.9), and rose more in the Loop than in the rest of the 'L' system.

graph_evidence.note: The graph is expected to hold no finding on the day-of-week pattern of transit ridership; see transit-weekday-pattern. Descriptive, run after the city test and not part of the verdict. For temperature concepts paired with violence-side concepts (homicide, assault, aggression, violent crime, suicide, injury, gun violence) and for telework or commuting variables, list every study behind the relationships (sysgraph.relationship_studies, sysgraph.study) and tabulate the population field by country and by setting. Predicted before the lookup: fewer than 25% of studies with a readable population name a US city or a US metropolitan area, fewer than 5 studies name Chicago or New York, and the telework and commuting findings are dominated by non-US samples (UK, Netherlands, China, Australia). The graph's population field is free text and sparse, so the share with a readable population is reported with the shares.

literature.citation: Barrero JM, Bloom N, Davis SJ (2023). The Evolution of Work from Home. Journal of Economic Perspectives 37(4):23-50.
literature.finding: Full days worked at home were 28% of paid workdays among Americans aged 20-64 in mid-2023, about four times the 2019 share (abstract).
literature.data_used: Survey of Working Arrangements and Attitudes (SWAA), monthly online survey of US residents, with ATUS and ACS for the pre-2020 series
literature.access_note: SWAA microdata are downloadable from wfhresearch.com; ACS and ATUS are public.

literature.citation: Barrero JM, Bloom N, Davis SJ (2021). Why Working from Home Will Stick. NBER Working Paper 28731.
literature.finding: Predicts that working from home will persist after the pandemic at a multiple of its 2019 level. Later SWAA releases and Bloom's public summaries name Friday as the most common day worked from home, with Monday and Thursday next; these day-of-week shares were read from secondary reports and slides, not from a table in the paper, so no number is quoted.

literature.citation: Light R, Osorio J, Liu Y, Ouyang Y (2025). How COVID-19 impacted Chicago Metra's ridership loss and recovery: 2019-2022. Transportation Research Part D 146:104857.
literature.finding: Attributes most of the weekday commuter-rail ridership loss to reduced workplace occupancy from remote work (abstract, read through a search summary). It does not report a day-of-week breakdown that we could verify.
literature.data_used: Metra station origin-destination ridership January 2019 to October 2022, workplace occupancy series

literature.citation: Kastle Systems. Back to Work Barometer (weekly, 2020-2026).
literature.finding: Office card-swipe occupancy in the New York metro area peaks on Tuesday and is lowest on Friday. Grey literature; the buildings are Kastle's clients, not a sample of offices. No figure is quoted because dated New York day-of-week values could not be verified.
literature.data_used: Kastle access-control swipes in client buildings

prediction.definitions: As in transit-weekday-pattern: R[w,d] is the sum of rides over the stations of the area for week w and weekday d; I[w,d] = R[w,d] / mean(R[w,Tue], R[w,Wed], R[w,Thu]); Deficit(d) = 1 - mean over weeks of I[w,d]; MF deficit = (Deficit(Mon) + Deficit(Fri)) / 2; Delta = MF deficit in the recent period minus MF deficit in 2019, in percentage points; 95% percentile intervals from 10,000 bootstrap resamples of weeks, separately in each period (seed 20261112).
prediction.magnitude: Loop Delta between 5 and 12 points, near 8. Loop recent MF deficit 10% to 18%; Loop 2019 MF deficit 3% to 8%; Loop midweek range at most 4 points; rest-of-system Delta between 2 and 7 points and smaller than the Loop's.
prediction.transfers_band: Loop Delta within 25% of New York's 8.7 points, that is between 6.5 and 10.9 points, with an interval that excludes 0.
prediction.support_if: Loop Delta in [6.5, 10.9] points and its 95% interval excludes 0 (verdict confirmed = transfers).
prediction.refute_if: Loop Delta below 4.4 or above 13.1 points (outside 50% of New York's), or its 95% interval includes 0 (verdict contested = does not transfer).
prediction.otherwise: A Loop Delta in [4.4, 6.5) or (10.9, 13.1], with interval excluding 0, gives unsettled (partial transfer).
prediction.secondary_not_decisive: (i) rest-of-system Delta smaller than the Loop's with non-overlapping point and interval midpoint; (ii) Loop recent midweek range <= 4 points; (iii) placebo 2019 minus 2018 within 1.5 points; (iv) sign agreement of the Loop and rest-of-system Delta with New York's.

datasets.5neh-572f: CTA - Ridership - 'L' Station Entries - Daily Totals (data.cityofchicago.org)
datasets.8pix-ypme: CTA - System Information - List of 'L' Stops (coordinates for the Loop rule)

plan.access: concord/socrata.py with concord.socrata.DOMAIN = https://data.cityofchicago.org set in the script.
plan.measure: Sum of `rides` (turnstile entries) by date over the stations of an area. Entries only; the dataset has no hours.
plan.area: Loop: the station map_ids in 8pix-ypme whose mean stop coordinates lie within latitude 41.8750 to 41.8870 and longitude -87.6345 to -87.6255 (this box holds the elevated Loop stations and the State and Dearborn subway stations from Lake to LaSalle/Van Buren; 15 stations). Rest of system: every other station_id in 5neh-572f. The list of station ids is written to the derived data before ridership is queried.
plan.periods: Recent: 2025-11-01 to 2026-10-31, or, if the dataset ends earlier, the latest twelve full calendar months it holds. Baseline: 2019-01-01 to 2019-12-31. Placebo year 2018.
plan.unit_and_exclusions: Identical to transit-weekday-pattern: a week (Monday to Sunday) is dropped if any day is an observed US federal holiday (Juneteenth from 2021), falls from 24 December to 1 January, or if its five weekdays are not all in the period. Dates are calendar dates.
plan.model: Ratios as defined, with a week bootstrap. No regression model.
sensitivity: S1 median across weeks in place of the mean
S2 drop only the holidays and 24 December to 1 January, keeping the rest of those weeks
S4 2019 baseline without the weeks of the Chicago Teachers Union strike (17 to 31 October 2019)
S5 station-level: the MF deficit computed for each Loop station, median and interquartile range
S6 Loop box widened to latitude 41.8740 to 41.8900 (adds Harrison, Grand/State)

alternatives: A Monday/Friday deficit before 2020 that differs between the cities for institutional reasons (office hours, schedules, school calendars).
CTA service levels on Mondays and Fridays and the 2019 teachers' strike, which affect entries independently of demand.
Different composition of the Loop: more tourists, Millennium Park and lakefront events, and student travel, which are spread differently over the week.
Station entries count transfers between lines only where a fare gate is crossed; the Loop's elevated stations have no free transfers between them.
Chicago's downtown has recovered less than New York's in level, so a given absolute remote-work day shifts the ratios more.
Weather, strikes and events that fall on particular weekdays by chance.
prior_note: The band is narrow and Chicago's level of office return is lower; the sign is likely right, the size less so.
seen_before_registration: No value from the Chicago portal (data.cityofchicago.org) had been queried by this project: data/cache/socrata holds no Chicago file and no script in analyses/ names a Chicago dataset. Before registering, this agent read (1) the catalog search results (dataset id, name, update time) for the four datasets named below, (2) the column lists and descriptions of gumc-mgzr, 5neh-572f, 8pix-ypme and ijzp-q8t2, and (3) for the CTA stops table 8pix-ypme the station names and coordinates of the 144 stations (used to fix the Loop rule; no ridership value). No row count, date range, shooting count, ridership value or temperature value for Chicago was read, and the Midway and O'Hare weather files were not opened. The NYC side was already known: the NYC estimates in the prediction are the project's own outcomes (heat-shootings, transit-weekday-pattern). For the weekday claim the agent also recomputed, from cached NYC queries only, the NYC Delta for the rest of the subway system (all complexes outside the CBD): 4.2 points (2.2 to 6.6), recent Monday/Friday deficit 7.3%, 2019 deficit 3.1%. The registrant knows from general reading that Chicago shootings peak in summer, that Chicago downtown office occupancy has recovered less than New York's, and the abstract of Reeping and Hemenway (2020).
